name: United Arab Emirates
governanceModel: State-directed strategy consolidated under a single new AI Authority
debateTopics: Consolidating AI governance under a single new Authority
Chip access — compute diplomacy vs. continued export friction
overview:
The UAE consolidated its AI governance in June 2026, approving a new Artificial Intelligence and Data Authority that merges the former Office of AI/Digital Economy/Remote Work Applications, the UAE Data Office, and the TDRA's digital-government portfolio into one body. Omar Sultan Al Olama, the UAE's Minister of State for AI, was confirmed as its chair — extending his existing mandate into a single, more powerful institution.

On the industry side, Abu Dhabi's G42 (roughly $20B) and the Technology Innovation Institute jointly produce the Falcon model family, including 2026 releases Falcon Perception (efficient multimodal) and Falcon-H1 Arabic, described as the world's leading Arabic-language LLM. Chip access remains a live and only partly resolved question: the US authorized G42 to purchase up to 35,000 NVIDIA Blackwell chips in November 2025, though some 2026 reporting suggests the UAE still faces friction in fully unrestricted access.

currentDirection.summary: The UAE is consolidating institutional control over AI policy under a single new Authority chaired by its long-standing AI minister — a centralising move even though no binding AI-specific law has followed, paired with continued heavy state investment in sovereign compute and Arabic-language frontier models.

debates.topic: Consolidating AI governance under a single new Authority
debates.summary: Merging three previously separate federal bodies into one Authority centralises AI policy — a significant institutional bet on unified control.
debates.expanded: Combining the AI office, Data Office, and TDRA's digital-government functions gives the new Authority broad reach across data governance, AI development, and remote-work policy. Supporters see this as removing coordination friction between previously siloed bodies; the concentration of power in one authority under one minister is itself a notable governance choice worth watching as it beds in.

debates.topic: Chip access — compute diplomacy vs. continued export friction
debates.summary: The US approved a major chip sale to G42 in late 2025, but 2026 reporting suggests the UAE still faces some friction in achieving fully unrestricted access to advanced AI hardware.
debates.expanded: The November 2025 approval for G42 to purchase up to 35,000 NVIDIA Blackwell chips was a major reversal of prior US reluctance, tied to Gulf 'compute diplomacy' and multibillion-dollar investment pledges. But subsequent 2026 analysis suggests US export rules still keep the UAE in what one report called an 'AI technology slow lane' in some respects — the picture is a live tension, not a fully resolved one.
